_comment: Living off the land. firewood: how easy it is to find fuel in each land (plenty/some/little/none). shelter: Survival DC to build a rough shelter (a lean-to, a hollow in the lee of rocks) in each land. forage: Survival DC to find something to eat (winter adds winter_dc), what you find (item, dice) and extras found on a good roll (item, dice, chance). hunt: Survival DC, and the game you might take: [name, weight, meat dice, hide item or null]. fish: DC and catch. cooking: what raw food becomes over a fire (needs_pot: needs a pot or mess kit).

torches.name: torches
torches.text: You split the wood, wrap the heads and make torches.

bandages.name: bandages
bandages.text: You tear the linen into strips and roll them.

splints.name: splints
splints.text: You cut and trim two splints, and pad them with what you have.

salted_meat.name: salted meat
salted_meat.text: You rub the meat with salt and pack it. It will keep now.

dried_fish.name: dried fish
dried_fish.text: You split the fish and hang them in the smoke until they are hard and dark.

remedy.name: a herbal remedy
remedy.text: You boil the herbs down to something bitter, dark and worth carrying.

acid_alchemy.name: acid
acid_alchemy.text: Salts and spirits boiled down into a corrosive that eats through metal and skin.

perfume_alchemy.name: perfume
perfume_alchemy.text: Crushed herbs steeped and distilled into a scent that hides a week on the road.

antitoxin_brewing.name: antitoxin
antitoxin_brewing.text: A bitter brew from fermented herbs that helps the body throw off a poison.

ladder_carpentry.name: ladder
ladder_carpentry.text: Rails and rungs pegged together into a ladder.

pole_carpentry.name: pole
pole_carpentry.text: A straight length of wood trimmed smooth for prodding at floors.

map_cartography.name: map
map_cartography.text: What you know of the land inked onto a scraped skin for someone else to follow.

arcane_focus_jewelling.name: arcane focus
arcane_focus_jewelling.text: A silver setting cut and polished to focus a caster's will.

holy_symbol_jewelling.name: holy symbol
holy_symbol_jewelling.text: Silver worked into a sign a believer can hold in a bad hour.

pouch_leatherwork.name: pouches
pouch_leatherwork.text: Hide cut, stitched and drawn with a thong into belt pouches.

quiver_leatherwork.name: quiver and bolt case
quiver_leatherwork.text: A stiff leather quiver and a flat case for crossbow bolts.

caltrops_smithing.name: caltrops
caltrops_smithing.text: Four-pointed iron cut and bent so that one point always stands up.

spikes_smithing.name: iron spikes
spikes_smithing.text: A bar drawn out and cut into spikes for wedging doors and pinning ropes.

chain_smithing.name: chain
chain_smithing.text: Links forged one by one and closed into a length of chain.

flask_tinkering.name: flasks
flask_tinkering.text: Beaten and soldered copper into small flasks with a tight stopper.

robe_weaving.name: robe
robe_weaving.text: Wool cloth cut and stitched into a long robe.

string_weaving.name: string
string_weaving.text: Linen unpicked and twisted into lengths of fine string.

net_weaving.name: net
net_weaving.text: Rope unlaid and knotted into a throwing net.

arrows_carving.name: arrows
arrows_carving.text: Straight shafts whittled, notched and fletched.

bolts_carving.name: bolts
bolts_carving.text: Short heavy bolts cut for a crossbow.

poison_poisoners.name: basic poison
poison_poisoners.text: Pressed herbs boiled down to a sticky poison for a blade.

antitoxin_herbalism.name: antitoxin
antitoxin_herbalism.text: Herbs steeped to a bitter draught against poison.

healers_kit_herbalism.name: healer's kit
healers_kit_herbalism.text: Herbs, dressings and a needle packed together for treating wounds.

any: Something moves out there, a long way off, and does not come back.
An owl, twice, and then nothing.
The wind gets up in the small hours and worries at everything that is not tied down.
You wake once, for no reason you can name, and lie listening until you don't.
Far off, a dog. Or something that wants to be taken for one.
The cold finds the gap between your cloak and the ground, and keeps it.
Rain starts on the canvas, or on your face, and you decide it is not worth moving for.
Somebody in the party talks in their sleep, a few words, and none of them are for you.
You lie awake doing sums about food and days, and get a different answer each time.
A fox screams, close, like a woman being murdered, and then goes about its evening.
fire: The fire ticks and settles, and throws a shape on the ground that is not there when you look.
You feed the fire at some hour and watch it take, which is worth doing for its own sake.
Sparks go up and out, and for a moment you can see nothing at all beyond them.
The fire burns down to a red eye and watches you back.
Green wood spits and a coal lands on your cloak; you brush it off before it wakes you properly.
The smoke changes its mind about which way to go, and finds you.
forest: The trees work all night, creaking and settling like a house.
Something small and busy goes through the leaf litter, over and over, until it stops.
An owl goes over, low, and you hear the air in its feathers.
A branch comes down somewhere with a long tearing crack and then silence.
Water drips off leaves for an hour after the rain has stopped.
Something walks a circle round the camp, well out, and does not come closer.
marsh: The frogs stop all at once, and start again, and you do not learn why.
Gas comes up out of the water somewhere and smells of the inside of a grave.
A bird you cannot name calls once an hour, all night, from a different place each time.
Mist comes up to knee height and stays there, moving without wind.
The ground under the bedroll is dry when you lie down and wet by morning.
A light shows out over the water and goes out when you sit up.
mountains: Stones go down a slope somewhere above you, and take a long time about it.
The cold up here has a smell to it, like iron and snow.
Wind comes down the valley in one piece, hits the camp, and goes on.
Ice cracks somewhere above, a sound like a door in an empty house.
The stars do not twinkle up here; they just sit there, hard and close.
You wake short of breath for no reason and take a while to settle.
tundra: The silence is complete enough to hear your own blood.
The sky is scoured clean and there are more stars than anybody could want.
The light never quite goes, and you sleep badly under it.
Frost forms on the outside of your blanket and on the inside of it.
Something crosses the snow a long way off, dark against white, and is gone.
The cold gets into the water skins; you break the skin of ice with your thumb.
plains: Grass, all night, moving like water.
A long way off, lights: a village, or somebody else's fire.
The horizon flickers with a storm too far off to hear.
Something big moves through the grass and never shows itself.
The wind lies down at midnight and the silence wakes you.
Dew comes down heavy and everything you own is damp by morning.
